title: Josip and Anna, with Ante
caption: A studio portrait: Josip seated in a light suit and loose cravat, Anna in a dark bodice with the high collar and gathered shoulders of the 1890s, the baby Ante across her lap in a striped romper. The painted backdrop and the vignetted edge are the marks of a small provincial photographer.
holder: Family collection (Omiš branch)

title: Zane Defranceschi
caption: A man in a white peaked cap, shirtsleeves and wide trousers, seated on a rush-bottomed chair against a whitewashed wall, a barefoot boy leaning on his shoulder. Zane is the Venetian form of Giovanni — the same name the parish clerks wrote as Zuane.
holder: Family collection (Omiš branch)

title: Zane, middle front
caption: A group photograph kept with the Omiš papers; the family's note places Zane in the middle of the front row.
holder: Family collection (Omiš branch)

title: Anton “Toni” Franceschi, 1932
caption: Dated by the family to 1932. Note the surname as written on the print: Franceschi, without the particle — the Omiš branch dropped and resumed it by turns.
holder: Family collection (Omiš branch)

title: Frane Defranceski
caption: Frane is the Croatian form of Francesco; the surname on this print is spelled the Croatian way, Defranceski.
holder: Family collection (Omiš branch)

title: Carlo De Franceschi in old age
caption: The historian of Istria, born at Gologorica in 1809, photographed late in life: round spectacles, white beard, dark stock. He died in 1893.
holder: Reproduced in the Seget monograph

title: Petar Defranceski — Fiche Individuelle
caption: The French-zone camp card. Petar, born 15 June 1913 at Crikvenica, Yugoslav, profession auto-mécanicien, employer's address Kelterstr. 30 Neuhausen, married. Five fingerprints in red, a passport photograph clipped at the top right, file 148.902 / 30609.
holder: International Tracing Service / Arolsen Archives

title: Zdrafko Defranceski — Fiche Individuelle
caption: Born 1 April 1921, Yugoslav, auto-mécanicien, married. File 148.901 / 30560. The same trade as Petar, and the same camp office.
holder: International Tracing Service / Arolsen Archives

title: Ruža Defranceski — Fiche Individuelle
caption: Born 1922, no profession recorded, married. In the photograph she wears a cross at her throat and holds her infant son, who is not named here: he is **Anton Mario De Franceski**, born 21 August 1944 at Reutlingen, who sailed with them to Australia at four and died in 1999. *This caption said «he was born in 1944 and may be living» long after the archive had his grave; corrected 23 September 2026.*
holder: International Tracing Service / Arolsen Archives

title: Foreigners registered at Pfullingen, 1939–45
caption: “Aufstellung über die in der Zeit vom 1. Sept. 1939 – 25. April 1945 in der Vorstadt Pfullingen gemeldet gewesenen Ausländer. Hier: Kroatien.” Drawn up at Reutlingen-Pfullingen on 10 March 1947. Six Defranceskis are listed, five of them born at Crikvenica.
holder: International Tracing Service / Arolsen Archives

title: ITS file cover D-1.505
caption: The tracing-service wrapper for the family: Petar, his wife Luise née Salzer of Neuhausen, and two daughters born at Urach and Metzingen during the war.
holder: International Tracing Service / Arolsen Archives

title: CM/1 application, identity page
caption: The IRO care-and-maintenance application, 7 November 1947. Petar gives his nationality at birth as Austria-Hungary, his address as Kelternstr. 30 Neuhausen, and the country he wants to be resettled in as the United States — California.
holder: International Tracing Service / Arolsen Archives

title: CM/1 application, history page
caption: Residences, trades and schooling: Split 1937–39 with Jugoslav Lloyd as a ship's engineer, then Germany from April 1939; car-mechanic examination at Reutlingen in 1947; a truck valued at 15,000 among his assets; and an aunt, Jacomina Alafetić, at San Pedro, California.
holder: International Tracing Service / Arolsen Archives

title: Felix Defranceski — sickness-fund card
caption: Felix, born 1908 at Crikvenica, single, living at Pfullingerlandstraße in Reutlingen. Employers from July 1941: Hermann Sauer of Pfullingen as a motor mechanic, then Wilhelm Heim as a driver, then Sauer again.
holder: International Tracing Service / Arolsen Archives

title: Ivan Defranceski — sickness-fund card
caption: Ivan, born June 1925 at Crikvenica, single, Brunnenstraße 7, Pfullingen. He entered work on 21 October 1941, aged sixteen, as a Hilfsarbeiter — an unskilled hand.
holder: International Tracing Service / Arolsen Archives

title: Petar Defranceski — sickness-fund card
caption: Marked “Kroate” in the top margin. Employed by Hermann Sauer of Reutlingen on motor-vehicle repairs from 1 April 1942 to 2 March 1945 — the card runs out three weeks before the French army reached the town.
holder: International Tracing Service / Arolsen Archives

title: Zdravko Defranceski — sickness-fund card
caption: Below the employment lines, a clerk has pencilled a short life: in Croatia 1936–43; taken by the Partisans in 1943; three or four months in captivity; then straight to Germany.
holder: International Tracing Service / Arolsen Archives

title: Anton Defranceski, born 1890 — municipal certificate
caption: Certified by the mayor of Pfullingen, Kreis Reutlingen, on 28 February 1950: Anton Defranceski, born 20 January 1890 at Crikvenica, Croatia-Yugoslavia, lodged at Pfullingen, workplace Hermann Sauer, Reutlingen-Süd.
holder: International Tracing Service / Arolsen Archives

title: Resettlement roll, February 1949
caption: Lines 58–60 of a nominal roll dated 22 February 1949: Zdrafko, Ruža and their son, Yugoslavs from Crikvenica and Fužine, at Reutlingen, with IRO numbers against each name.
holder: International Tracing Service / Arolsen Archives

title: Državni arhiv u Pazinu to David Defranceski, 26 April 2021
caption: The Pazin State Archive answers a request made eight days earlier: the copy from the Gračišće birth register for Josip Defranceschi is enclosed. Itemised at 117 kuna — research 50, certified A3 copy 7, overseas postage 60.
holder: Državni arhiv u Pazinu (DAPA)

title: Liber Baptizatorum, Gračišće 1841–1899
caption: Certified and stamped by the Pazin State Archive. The register is ruled for house number, the child's name and date of birth, religion, sex, legitimacy, both parents with the father's condition, the godparents and the midwife. The entry taken out for this family is Josephus, born 22 March 1863, son of Antonius Defranceschi, lapicida — a stonecutter.
holder: Državni arhiv u Pazinu (DAPA), MKR Gračišće 1841–1899

title: Državni arhiv u Pazinu, 24 June 2021
caption: A second answer, this time for Antonius Defranceschi and his family, and for Giovanni Battista Defranceschi and his family — the two Status Animarum entries opposite. 124 kuna.
holder: Državni arhiv u Pazinu (DAPA)

title: Status Animarum — house 5, Gallignana
caption: The book of souls for the parish of Gallignana. House 5: Joan. Bapt. Defranceschi, agricola, born 13 August 1787, married 1819, died 1 September 1846; his wife Francisca Salomon, born 17 March 1797; and their sons Raymundus, Antonius, Joannes and Franciscus.
holder: Državni arhiv u Pazinu (DAPA), ZM34K 217, M01072071

title: Status Animarum — house 19, Gallignana
caption: House 19: † Antonius Defranceschi q. Joannis — son of the late Giovanni — born 20 September 1825, married 25 November 1856, died 4 August 1894; his wife Maria née Fernasar, born 17 October 1832; and their children Antonius, Josephus, Leopolda, Catharina and Modestus.
holder: Državni arhiv u Pazinu (DAPA), ZM34K 217, M01071656

title: Anna Kalanj, born 3 January 1864
caption: Entry 2 for 1864 in the baptismal register of Ledenice, the Vinodol parish above Crikvenica. Anna, legitimate, daughter of Josephus Kalanj and Rosalia née Perković, at Klenovica house 22; godparents Josephus Ban and his wife Anna; baptised by Vincentius Segulja, parish priest. The other entries on the page are Perković, Butković, Mataija, Semper — the surnames of one valley.
holder: Državni arhiv / matične knjige, Ledenice

title: Carlo De Franceschi signs as a witness, Pazin 1842
caption: The Pisino marriage register, 13 September 1842. Antonius Covach, 22, of house 33, marries Hedwiges Mrak, 17, of house 30. In the column for witnesses: «Carolus Defranceschi» and «Aegidius Mrach», and against their names their conditions — «I. R. Auscultans» and «studiosus». Imperial-Royal Auscultator was the entry rank of the Austrian judicial service. Carlo was thirty-two.
holder: Hrvatski državni arhiv, HDA 583

title: Anton Rudolf, born 20 January 1890
caption: The whole opening, pages 124–125, in place of the single strip this site carried before. Entry 9, the last on the page: Anton Rudolf, born 20 January 1890, baptised 9 February, legitimate, son of «Josip Defranceschi i žena Ana Kalanj rodjena». Residence «Klenovica kbr. 22», written over «Gallignana u Istriji — za vičajno mjesto roditelja», Gallignana in Istria as the parents' place of settlement. Godfather Jakov Kalanj of that same house 22 — his mother's people — with Pavlina Trković; baptised by Matej Butković, parish priest. The full page adds three things the strip cut off. In pencil above the child's name, in a later hand: «vjenčao se na Crikvenici», he married at Crikvenica. In the remarks column, why the birth happened here at all: «Roditelji djeteta nahodeć se kod svojih u Klenovici, t.j. kod roditelja žene Ane, dobiše ovo djete, koje je u ovoj župnoj crkvi i kršteno» — the child's parents, being with their own people at Klenovica, that is with the parents of the wife Ana, had this child, and it was baptised in this parish church. And down the outer margin, the printer's line: «Tisak H. Luster u Senju» — printed by H. Luster at Senj.
holder: Matične knjige, Ledenice / Klenovica

title: Nodburga Defranceschi marries at Bakar, 1794
caption: 27 February 1794, dispensed from the third banns by the Bishop: in the church of the Blessed Virgin Mary, the marriage of Dominus Joannes Vorkret and Domicella Nodburga Defranceschi, blessed by Canon Antonius de Agnesis, in the presence of the Vice-Governor Aloysius de Orlando and the noble Antonio Maria ab Orebich, assessor of the community of Buccari. Notburga is a Tyrolean saint's name, and an odd one to find on the Kvarner coast.
holder: Matične knjige, Bakar (Buccari)

title: Antonio Defranceschi of Zara — refused
caption: A second IRO application, completed at Bolzano on 10 May 1950. Antonio Defranceschi, born 18 January 1905 at Zara, ethnic group Italian, son of Riccardo and Giuseppina Zersuscek; his wife Antonietta née Stipanovich, born 1910, daughter of Sabino Stipanovich and Maria Lovrich. Clerk at Zara to 1941, then a soldier in the Italian army until the capitulation, then Zara again until January 1944, then Italy. Twice across the form, in blue crayon: NOT WITHIN THE MANDATE OF IRO.
holder: International Tracing Service / Arolsen Archives

title: Edoardo De Franceschi dies at San Daniele del Friuli, 1899
caption: Atti di morte no. 28, San Daniele del Friuli, 12 August 1899: at five in the morning there died in the Civic Hospital «De Franceschi Edoardo, di anni quarantotto, già Ufficiale, nato in Zara e domiciliato in Zara, figlio del fu Giovanni e della fu Zenardi Maria, coniugato a Pappafava Regina» — a former officer of Zadar, forty-eight, seven hundred kilometres from home.
holder: Comune di San Daniele del Friuli, Atti di morte

title: Pietro De Franceschi dies at San Daniele del Friuli, 1895
caption: Atti di morte no. 19, 30 March 1895, in the same hospital four years earlier: «De Franceschi Pietro, di anni quarantaquattro, mura…» — a mason, forty-four. The trade of the Gračišće line, in the country the family says it came from.
holder: Comune di San Daniele del Friuli, Atti di morte

title: Josip Defranceski — of the Imotski branch, not this line
caption: A hand-tinted studio portrait: dark hair swept back, a full beard, a bow tie. **This archive published it as Josip Defranceschi of Crikvenica, born at Gračišće in 1863 — David's great-grandfather. That was wrong.** The photograph belongs to the **Imotski** branch and the sitter is a Josip of that family, not of this line. The mistake is David's own family collection having the two branches' pictures in one place, and this archive assuming the face on a card matched the name it was filed under. **No likeness of the Crikvenica Josip is known to this archive.** Corrected 9 September 2026 on David's identification.
holder: Family collection (Imotski branch)

title: Ana — the companion portrait, now unidentified
caption: A young woman in a high-necked dress with lace at the cuffs, hair dressed up, hand resting on a chair back, tinted the same warm brown by the same hand. **Its whole identification rested on being the matched half of the portrait beside it** — and that man has turned out to be an Imotski Josip, not the Crikvenica one. So this is very probably his wife and of the same branch, but this archive is not going to name her a second time on the strength of the reasoning that failed the first. **Unidentified until someone who holds the originals says otherwise.** *(open)*
holder: Family collection — branch now uncertain

title: The grave of Ana de Franceschi
caption: A standing stone with a cross and two oval porcelain medallions — a woman, and a man in a fedora. «Ovdje počiva u miru Božjem — ANA DE. FRANCESCHI — ✱ 19.IX.1863 ✝ 28.V.1936». Here rests in God's peace. Below the dates the word «suprug», husband, begins a second inscription that the photograph cuts off.
holder: Family collection (Crikvenica)

title: Ursula, born Kovačina
caption: Anton Rudolf's wife, and the mother of the four brothers who ended up in Württemberg. Seated, in the loose drop-waisted dress of the early 1920s, something folded in her lap. The print is worn to the emulsion at every corner.
holder: Family collection (Crikvenica)

title: Ursula in old age, with a grandchild
caption: Colour, 1960s or 70s. She sits among stacked café chairs on a seafront, a small child standing against her knee, a traffic policeman in white passing behind. The child is not named here.
holder: Family collection (Crikvenica)

title: Petar Defranceski
caption: A studio portrait in a double-breasted pinstripe. Set this beside the photograph clipped to his French camp card in 1947 and it is plainly the same man: the same long jaw, the same swept hair.
holder: Family collection (Crikvenica)

title: “Peter (Senior), pilot in war”
caption: A young man in a leather flying helmet with the goggles pushed up on his forehead, and a sheepskin-collared flying jacket. The family's own caption calls him Peter Senior, a pilot in the war. Nothing in the displaced-persons file mentions flying: there he is a ship's engineer with Jugoslav Lloyd, and then a motor mechanic.
holder: Family collection (Crikvenica)

title: Zdravko Defranceski
caption: A studio portrait in a wide-lapelled pinstripe suit, hair oiled back — the same face as the French camp card of 1947, a few years and a good deal of trouble apart.
holder: Family collection (Crikvenica)

title: Zdravko's plaque at Horsham
caption: «IN LOVING REMEMBRANCE OF ZDRAVKO FRANK DEFRANCESKI — DIED 22ND DECEMBER 1979 AGED 58 — BELOVED HUSBAND OF ROSA» — and then his two children and his four grandchildren, who are living and are not named here — «RESTING IN GOD'S LOVING CARE.» A bronze plaque set flush in a concrete surround in a lawn cemetery in the Victorian Wimmera, for a man born on the Kvarner. Aged 58 in December 1979 puts his birth in 1921, which is the year the family gives. This is the camera original, four times the size of the copy that was in the family tree file: the founder's mark in the bottom right corner, «C2110», is now legible.
holder: Family collection

title: Ruža, born Hreljac
caption: A young woman with a flower pinned in her hair, photographed in the 1940s. Born at Fužine on 13 February 1922; died 30 January 1996 and buried at Horsham beside Zdravko.
holder: Family collection

title: The grave of Ivan Defrančeski, 1925–1995
caption: Polished dark granite, a gilt cross, a lantern, and the name in gilt letters in Croatian orthography: IVAN DEFRANČESKI, and beneath it 1925 and 1995. The dates are now legible — the copy this site had before was 400 pixels wide and they were not. The slab immediately behind is a RUKAVINA, a Senj and Lika name. The boy who entered a Reutlingen factory at sixteen in October 1941 went home, and is buried on his own coast; his son's birth certificate of 1951, also on this page, gives his trade as electro-mechanic and his citizenship as stateless.
holder: Family collection

title: Anton, as a boy
caption: The child written on the French camp card in 1947 with the single word «enfant» across the fingerprint boxes, and photographed that year in his mother's arms. Here he is a few years older, in a dark pinafore over a knitted jumper. The print is torn across one corner. He died at Ipswich, Queensland, in 1999.
holder: Family collection

title: Pepe, centre, with four sailors
caption: Five young men in naval ratings' uniform and round caps, shoulder to shoulder against a hedge. The family caption puts Pepe in the middle. Interwar, and the Adriatic: these are Yugoslav navy caps.
holder: Family collection (Crikvenica)

title: Pepe on the sea wall
caption: A man in shirtsleeves sitting on a harbour parapet, a bay and a low waterfront behind him, boats out on the water. The photographer's blindstamp in the corner reads ZORA.
holder: Family collection (Crikvenica)

title: Stancija Seghetto — the manor house
caption: The front Giorgio de Franceschi (1788–1865) commissioned in 1843–45: two giant pilasters flanking the centre, two orders of six windows, a great round-arched portal, and a tympanum over all. Neoclassical, in the manner of the second quarter of the nineteenth century, grafted onto a Venetian country house of the seventeenth.
holder: Family collection (Seget)

title: The arms in the tympanum
caption: A circular medallion set in the pediment, with a shield carved in relief inside it, and below, lozenge panels with rosettes. La Voce del popolo records the arms here as «troncato di azzurro e d'oro al leone rampante al naturale». At this resolution the carving cannot be read as heraldry — the shape of a shield is legible and nothing inside it is. A proper photograph would settle it.
holder: Family collection (Seget)

title: The crenellated tower
caption: «La torre con merlature, ubicata a nord-ovest rispetto alla casa dominicale» — the battlemented tower north-west of the manor, built to watch the property, and badly restored at the end of the twentieth century. It stands at the roadside with a vine over its shoulder.
holder: Family collection (Seget)

title: The rustic range behind the house
caption: Arcaded outbuildings in bad repair: the coach house, the produce stores and the colonists' dwellings. The nineteenth-century oil mill stood among these, with its presses and a dozen stone oil jars, until it was converted into a house about twenty years ago.
holder: Family collection (Seget)

title: The well
caption: A stone wellhead with an iron arch over it, in what is now a garden. The whole holding was walled, and this stood inside it.
holder: Family collection (Seget)

title: The Mione birth index, 1806–1810
caption: «Dipartimento di Passariano, Distretto di Tolmezzo, Cantone di Rigolato, Comune di Mione — Tavola alfabetica per gli Atti di Nascita ch'ebbero luogo dall'anno 1806 all'anno 1810.» The first three lines of the alphabet are Defranceschi Anna-Maria, Defranceschi Anna-Cecilia and De Franceschi Gio: Batta. Four Erman entries follow a few lines down — the other family named in the headmen's list of 1679.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, sig. 12954

title: Anna Maria de Franceschi, Muina, 30 December 1809
caption: Act 32, the last of the year. The midwife Speranza, wife of Antonio Galante, aged fifty-nine, of Muina, presented a girl born that morning at eleven, named Anna Maria — daughter of «Osvaldo de Franceschi e di Appolonia Galante sua consorte, ambedue agricoltori domiciliati in esso villaggio». Registrar: Giacomo Micoli.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Nati 1809

title: Anna Cecilia de' Franceschi, Mione, 14 January 1810
caption: Act 1 of 1810. «Francesco de' Franceschi d'anni ventisei circa, di professione Sarto» — a tailor, aged about twenty-six — brought his daughter, born that morning at three, and named her Anna Cecilia; her mother is «Margherita nata Gortan sua consorte». He signs the register himself. Act 2 below names Pasqua de' Franceschi, wife of Pietro Luchin of Mione.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Nati 1810

title: Giovanni Battista De Franceschi, Mione, 15 October 1810
caption: Act 21. «De Franceschi Osualdo d'anni ventisei, di professione fa legname» — a carpenter — presented his son, born at ten that morning in the contrada of Mione, and named him Gio: Batta. The mother is «Cattarina nata Brencis sua consorte». Witnesses: a shoemaker and a tailor, both of Luint. He signs.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Nati 1810

title: The Mione marriage index, 1806–1810
caption: Two De Franceschi marriages in one small book. The first line of the alphabet: «Galante Appolonia con Defranceschi Osualdo — di Muina — 28 Gennajo 1808». Further down: «Prencis Valentina con Defranceschi Osualdo — di Mione — 6 Agosto 1807».
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, sig. 12987

title: Osvaldo de Franceschi marries Appolonia Galante, 28 January 1808
caption: The deepest document in this archive. Osvaldo de Franceschi, farmer, aged twenty, of Muina, «figlio di Antonio de Franceschi, e di Maria nata Corva, pure agricoltori», marries Appolonia Galante, aged twenty-five and a half, daughter of Antonio Galante and Speranza née Micoli. His birth act is read out: born 14 March 1788 at Muina, «da legittimo Matrimonio di Antonio qm. Leonardo de Franceschi, e di Maria nata Corva» — Antonio, son of the late Leonardo. His father's written consent is dated 25 October 1807. Four witnesses, three of them Micoli of Muina. Both spouses sign.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Matrimoni 1808, atto 1

title: Giacoma de Franceschi marries, 7 August 1806
caption: The earliest De Franceschi act found in Carnia. At Mione, in the «Distretto della Carnia, Cantone di Gorto», Giacoma de Franceschi — seventeen years, two months and twelve days old, «figlia del fu Osualdo de Franceschi, e di Catterina nata Fabris» — marries Ignazio di Prato, a merchant of Chialina. Her birth act of 25 May 1789 is read into the record. She signs herself «Giacoma de Franceschi q.m Osualdo». All four witnesses are tailors; the registrar is Giovanni Micoli-Toscano and the secretary Battà Micoli-Toscano.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Matrimoni 1806

title: The Mione death index, 1806–1810
caption: Eight Defranceschi entries: Maria 1807, Lucia and Francesco Antonio 1808, Leonarda 1808, Anna Cecilia in January 1810 eleven days after her birth, Sebastiano «chierico» in July 1810, Maddalena in August and Mariana in September. Corva and Erman entries stand among them.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, sig. 12966

title: The parish certificate of 1806, reaching back to 1789
caption: Filed with the marriage as an allegato, under a two-and-sixpence revenue stamp of the Kingdom of Italy: «Certifico io sottoscritto Parroco della Pieve Matrice di Gorto a parte Luvincis, come Giacoma figlia legitima e naturale di OSUALDO QUONDAM GIO: BATTA DE' FRANCESCHI DI MIONE, e di Cattarina sua moglie, essa è nata li 25 del mese di Maggio nell'anno 1789, come consta dal Libro dei Battezzi.» Signed and sealed by D. Gio: Batta Dario, pievano, at Luincis on 5 August 1806, and countersigned at Mione by the mayor Giovanni Micoli-Toscano.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Matrimoni allegati 1806

title: A notary's extract from Chialina, 8 October 1805
caption: Catterina, widow of the late Gio: Giacomo di Prato of Chialina, could not attend the signing of the marriage contract between her son Ignazio and «Giacoma figlia di D.no Osualdo de' Franceschi di Mione», so she appeared before the notary and declared her assent. Drawn by Antonio di Prato, notary. Note the style given to Giacoma's father: Dominus.
holder: Archivio di Stato di Udine, Stato civile napoleonico, Mione, Matrimoni allegati 1806

title: Yugoslav nationals resident at Reutlingen
caption: Not the Pfullingen list, but the town's own: «Liste der im Stadtgebiet Reutlingen mit Betzingen und Sondelfingen wohnhaft gewesenen jugoslavischen Staatsangehörigen». Line 16 is Defranceski Felix, born 14.1.08 at Crikvenica, present from 15 August 1941 to 8 October 1942. Read the lines around him: Brozicevic, Car, three Domijans and Dracic, every one of them born at Crikvenica, arriving from October 1938.
holder: Arolsen Archives, DE ITS 2.1.3.1 BW 029 7 JUG ZM

title: Petar decides to stay — the counselling card, 1949–51
caption: A resettlement counselling card for Peter and Luise Defranceski, IRO 148.902, at Kelternstraße 30, Neuhausen. Three lines under EXPOSÉ settle what became of the plan to go to California. 22 July 1949: «Veut rester en Allemagne, a une maison, 2 autos etc.» — wants to stay in Germany, has a house, two cars. 28 April 1951: confirms the family wish to remain. 25 May 1951: listed among displaced persons living privately.
holder: Arolsen Archives, ITS 3.1.1.1, folder DP0758

title: Petar's camp card — the original
caption: The same Fiche Individuelle the family holds as a faint photocopy, here in the original: the clipped passport photograph legible, the five fingerprints in red, «Auto-mecancien», Kelterstr. 30 Neuhausen, file 148.902 CB and 30609.
holder: Arolsen Archives, ITS 3.1.1.1, folder DP0758

title: Felix's sickness-fund card — the green original
caption: The Allgemeine Ortskrankenkasse membership and benefit card in its original green, stamped DOCUMENT EXPLOITÉ. Felix Defranceski, born 14.1.08 at Ericvenica, single, of Reutlingen, Pfullingerlandstraße. Four employments between July 1941 and October 1942, three of them for Hermann Sauer.
holder: Arolsen Archives, ITS 2.2.2.1 War Time Card File

title: The Pfullingen list, with the dates readable
caption: The same list of 10 March 1947 the family holds, but the Arolsen original. Six Defranceski with their arrival and departure dates: Felix from 5 July 1941; Ivan from 20 October 1941 to 5 September 1942; Anton, born 20.1.90, from 1 March to 13 June 1942 only; Zdravko from 17 June 1944; Ruža of Fužine from 29 July 1944. Felix, Zdravko and Ruža all leave on the same day — 3 March 1945.
holder: Arolsen Archives, DE ITS 2.1.3.1, ITS 154

title: The Neuhausen list, 25 March 1947
caption: Drawn up under General Koenig's Order No. 1792: every foreigner in the commune of Neuhausen an der Erms between September 1939 and April 1945. The first seven names are one family. Peter from 22 March 1941; Luise née Salzer, born in the village, «seit Geburt»; the daughters Ursula and Renate likewise; and Zdravko, Rose née Hreljec of Fužine/Belnica, and the infant Anton, all from 19 March 1945.
holder: Arolsen Archives, DE ITS 2.1.3.1, ITS 157

title: The Omiš descent chart
caption: A hand-compiled chart of the Omiš and Zadar family, twenty generations deep, running from the fourteenth century to the twentieth. The later generations are omitted from this archive because the people in them may be living.
holder: Family collection (Omiš branch)

title: Defranceschi at Bakar, 1783
caption: A register page kept with the family's research notes, placing the name at Bakar on the Kvarner coast in 1783.
holder: Family research collection

title: Moncalvo di Pisino

title: Il giovine Pensiero, Pola, 16 January 1895
caption: Front page. The stenographic record of the opening of the Provincial Diet of Istria at Parenzo. The provincial captain gives the floor to «l'on. Giovanni Battista de Franceschi, che a nome della maggioranza intera cosi si esprime» — and the speech that follows protests to the Imperial Government at the treatment of the Italians of Istria. Further down the same page, among the bills before the session: the establishment of new local communes at Pisino, Novacco, Lindaro, Terviso, Gallignana and Pedena.
holder: Osterreichische Nationalbibliothek, ANNO — igp18950116

title: The same issue, page two
caption: The motions and their signatories. G. B. de Franceschi signs the interpellation on the missing vice-president and Dr Bubba's motion against the bilingual signs in the Istrian district courts. Later he acts as teller in the election of a substitute assessor, and speaks again for the majority asking the Captain to talk the resigning assessors into staying.
holder: Osterreichische Nationalbibliothek, ANNO — igp18950116

title: L'Eco di Pola, 14 January 1893, page two
caption: Carlo De Franceschi's career obituary, six days after his death at Gologorica. It gives the reason he lost his post — «venne cassato dal ruolo degli impiegati e messo in quiescenza per sospetti politici», struck off the roll of officials and pensioned off on suspicion of political sympathies, in 1854 — and lists what he left unpublished: a volume of memoirs and an unfinished study on the nationality of Istria. The memoirs waited thirty-three years for his son Camillo to print them.
holder: Osterreichische Nationalbibliothek, ANNO — edp18930114

title: Il giovine Pensiero, 18 January 1893, front page
caption: Two things on one page. Top left, the life: «nacque a Moncalvo (Gollogorizza) il 17 Ottobre 1810 da famiglia abbastanza agiata» — a birth date ten days after his death that disagrees with the 16 October 1809 the reference books give, and the only contemporary word this archive holds on the standing of the household. Right-hand columns, the letter from Pisino signed Don Ramiro: «Sor Carlo» on a Saturday in the fountain square, surrounded by the poor of the commune, handing out alms and staying to talk.
holder: Osterreichische Nationalbibliothek, ANNO — igp18930118

title: Nasa Sloga, 25 March 1909, front page
caption: The Croatian paper of Istria answering the Italian side with the Italian side's own book. Middle of the page: «mjesta Gologorica, Cernogradus i Bellegradus spominju se u listini od 1102 (v. De Franceschi str. 351.)» — the places Gologorica, Cernogradus and Bellegradus are named in a charter of 1102, see De Franceschi page 351. Carlo had cited those same three names to argue the Slavs arrived late. Nasa Sloga cites them to argue the Croats were there first. The family's village is the first exhibit in both cases.
holder: Osterreichische Nationalbibliothek, ANNO — nsp19090325

title: Nasa Sloga, 13 April 1900, page two
caption: A false lead, kept because a negative result is a result. Among the local notices: «Nacelnikom u Umagu bijase izabran dne 9. t. mj. g. Fr. de Franceschi, bivsi nacelnik one obcine» — a Fr. de Franceschi elected mayor of Umag on 9 April 1900, having held the office before. Umag is at the far western tip of Istria, ninety kilometres from Gologorica, and nothing yet connects him to this family.
holder: Osterreichische Nationalbibliothek, ANNO — nsp19000413

title: Il giovine Pensiero, 26 July 1894, page two
caption: Correspondence datelined Moncalvo, dist. di Pisino, 24 July. The amateur band and many townspeople of Pisino came out on the Sunday, invited by the whole village, to the birthplace of Carlo De Franceschi. Two stones, apparently thrown from the bell tower, smashed the flower vase the village women had brought and crushed a trumpet; at half past eight the band tried to leave and was set on at the village exit by about ten men with stones and drawn blades. Fifteen wounded. The two hurt worst were carried into the Peschle house and the Defranceschi house, and four gendarmes came out from Pisino that night with the district doctor. The paper records, twice, that the communal representative Ivic was the same man who had refused burial to Carlo's body the year before -- and that none of the attackers was a native of Moncalvo.
holder: Osterreichische Nationalbibliothek, ANNO — igp18940726

title: Il giovine Pensiero, 15 June 1895, page three
caption: The trial of the band night, taken down witness by witness. Right-hand column: «Entra Vittorio Defranceschi fu Francesco, Gollogorizza d'anni 23» -- Vittorio Defranceschi, son of the late Francesco, of Gologorica, aged twenty-three, so born about 1872. He appears in other men's evidence as well. The shouts the court was trying to fix were «crepa i taliani, bastonemoli» and «zivio», and the advocate Dr Trinajstic addressed the bench in Croatian.
holder: Osterreichische Nationalbibliothek, ANNO — igp18950615

title: The builder's tablet, on the front of the house
caption: A plain rectangular panel of pale limestone set flush into the whitewashed wall under a moulded cornice, its cut letters shallow and raked by flat light. This is the stone that reads ANNO · DOMNI · 1711 / GION · BATISTA / DE · FRANCESCHI / FECCE · FARE · PE[R] · SE / ET · HEREDI · SVOI — the year Carlo gave Kobler privately in about 1873, cut in the wall of the house.
holder: Photographed by the family at Gologorica, 2026

title: The memorial to Carlo, under a shield
caption: A tall slab with a triangular pediment carrying a carved shield, and beneath it the inscription cut in Roman capitals for Carlo De Franceschi — «in questa casa avita nacque e morì», in this ancestral house he was born and died. The stone calls him patriotta fervente, archeologo e storico, and gives MDCCCIX–MDCCCXCIII.
holder: Photographed by the family at Gologorica, 2026

title: The arms, and the Madonna beneath them
caption: The two carvings in one frame, as they sit on the façade: above, an oval cartouche in high relief with curling mantling and a plumed helm; below it an aedicule with scrolled volutes and a moulded cornice, framing a marble relief of a haloed woman with her arms flung wide and drapery falling around her. Around the rim of the oval runs a circular legend of which «…A · DE · FRANCESCHI · FIERI…» survives.
holder: Photographed by the family at Gologorica, 2026

title: The blazon, cut in stone on the tomb
caption: In the pediment of the family tomb, a shield under a coronet: a cross rising the height of the field, crossed diagonally by two straight shafts, with a band beneath them. Set this beside what Carlo wrote to Giovanni Kobler in about 1873 — «nella parte superiore dello scudo una croce greca attraversata da due frecce, nell'inferiore un pomo granato; sopra lo scudo un elmo piumato». The description and the carving agree.
holder: Photographed by the family at Gologorica, 2026

title: The same arms, worn almost away
caption: An older stone in the same ground, its oval field weathered nearly smooth, with the cross and the crossing shafts still legible and something round below them where the pomegranate should be. Two carvings of one blazon, a century or more apart, on two stones in the same cemetery.
holder: Photographed by the family at Gologorica, 2026

title: The family tomb at Gologorica
caption: A tall stone monument with a cross on its gable, a panelled front of veined marble between pilasters, and the shield in the pediment; a plain cross stands to the left of it. This is the plot for which the architect Giuseppe Hirsch drew a «Cappella della famiglia di Carlo de Franceschi nel cimitero di Moncalvo di Pisino», the rolled plan for which is still in the Zagreb archive boxes.
holder: Photographed by the family at Gologorica, 2026

title: The house, from the lane

title: Giovanni Battista Defranceschi marries at Bakar, 20 November 1772
caption: The fourth entry on the left-hand page: «Die 20 9bris per dispensationem [D]omi[nicalem] Nuptijs in facie Ecclesiae contractis inter D. Joannem Bapt. filium D. Francisci Defranceschi et Catharinam filiam Def[uncti] Antonij Akacich benedixit D. Can[onicu]s Georgius Akacich, praesentibus Ill[ustrissi]mo DD. Antonio Viviani Vicario et Fiscali et Andrea Zergolech» — on 20 November, by dispensation, a marriage contracted in the face of the Church between Dominus Giovanni Battista, son of Dominus Francesco Defranceschi, and Catharina, daughter of the late Antonio Akačić; blessed by Canon Georgius Akačić, in the presence of the Most Illustrious Antonio Viviani, Vicar and Fiscal, and Andrea Zergolech. The bride’s surname is hard on the page; the FamilySearch index of the same volume reads it Akacich, and the canon who blessed the marriage carries it too, so a priest of her own family married her. title: Ivan on the shingle, about a year old
caption:
A baby sitting unaided on a shore of broken white limestone, bare but for a polka-dot kerchief knotted over his head against the sun, the exposed roots of a tree filling the frame behind him. He is laughing at something off to his right. **He can sit up without support and has his front teeth**, which puts him at roughly nine to eighteen months.

**⚠ The scan's own metadata dates this 31 December 1951, and that cannot be right.** Ivan was born on **17 December 1951**; on 31 December he was **fourteen days old**. The file's `DateTimeOriginal` reads `1951:12:31 14:00:00` — a round hour on the last day of the year, which is the shape of a date somebody typed to stand for «1951», not one a camera wrote. *The filename carries a third answer again, the prefix* `1990s_`, *which is the scanning batch.*

**Read from the photograph instead: a warm month, a child of about one — so the summer of 1952, or the summer of 1953 at the latest.** *(inf, from apparent age and bare skin; the 1951 stamp is **rejected**.)*
holder: Family collection — Cheryl's Album 2, leaf 209

title: Ivan as a young man, studio portrait
caption:
Head and shoulders against a studio backdrop graded from pale at the left to dark behind the right shoulder — the standard lighting of a small commercial studio. An open-necked white shirt with a broad soft collar, worn without a tie; dark hair brushed into a heavy wave off the forehead; the beginnings of a moustache. He looks just past the camera. **A rust-coloured foxing spot has bloomed on the print at the left collar point**, and the white border is trimmed close.

**Undated.** The file's timestamp, 19 January 2022, is **the date of the scan** — there is no camera make or model in it, and the image is a flatbed capture of a paper print. *From apparent age alone he is about sixteen to twenty, which would put the sitting somewhere around 1968 to 1971.* **(inf, and from the face only — no inscription, no studio stamp, nothing on the back has been read.)**
holder: Family collection — Cheryl's Album 4, leaf 69

title: Ivan at sixty, 12 April 2012
caption:
A close portrait lit from the left against a dark room, white hair back off the forehead, a white moustache and a small beard under the lip, the skin of the face carrying every line the light can find. He is looking straight into the lens and half-smiling.

**This one is dated to the minute and the date is the camera's own.** The file is `DSC_0843`, written by a **Nikon D800** — `DateTimeOriginal 2012:04:12 07:54:28`, **f/16, ISO 125, 135 mm**. *(doc: an EXIF date written by the camera at the moment of capture is evidence in a way a scan's timestamp never is.)*

**He was sixty years and four months old.**
holder: Family collection

title: Luiza Defranceski — Fiche Individuelle
caption:
«NOM **DEFRANCESKI** · PRÉNOMS **Luiza** · Nationalité **Youg.** · Date de naissance **5.10.1919** · Profession **ménagère** · Adresse de l'employeur **Neuhausen, Kelterstr. 30** · Situation de famille **mariée**» — IRO no. 148.902 B, camp number 31163.

**She is Petar's wife, and the address proves it before the names do.** *Kelterstr. 30 Neuhausen* is the employer's address on [Petar Defranceski](/person/petar-defranceski-1913/)'s own fiche. This archive already knew he *«married **Luise Salzer** at Neuhausen in February 1942»* — **this is that woman, under her married name, with her own date of birth on a card of her own.** *(doc.)*
holder: Arolsen Archives
note: **Arolsen Archives**, French-zone IRO records for the Reutlingen–Pfullingen camps, file **148.902**. Supplied by David, 23 September 2026.

title: Luiza's identity card — and the only picture of the children
caption:
**Carte d'identité de Personnes Déplacées**, *Commandement en Chef Français en Allemagne*, issued **27 November 1948**. Nom **DEFRANCESKI**, prénom **Lujza**, Yougoslave, **Neuhausen, Kelterstr. 30, Cercle de Reutlingen**, mariée. Her thumbprint in the box, the French zone's stamp across the photograph.

**In the photograph she is holding two small children.** *They are named on cards of their own in the same file and they are not named here, because both were born within living memory and this archive does not print a living person's date of birth — not in text and not in a scan of a document that states it.* **The photograph is published; their two fiches are not.**
holder: Arolsen Archives
note: **Arolsen Archives**, French-zone IRO records for the Reutlingen–Pfullingen camps, file **148.902**. Supplied by David, 23 September 2026.

title: The letter that let them stay
caption:
**International Refugee Organization, Zone Française d'Occupation en Allemagne**, to the Chef de Service du Wurtemberg. *«OBJET: Cas de **DEFRANCESKI** … Je vous informe que l'éligibilité de l'intéressé a été vérifiée le **15.12.48**. Le Chef de famille et les **deux enfants** sont classés **B**, l'épouse **BC**.»*

**Eligibility was the whole question for a displaced person**: it decided whether the IRO would feed you, house you and resettle you, or whether you were a foreign national who could be sent home. **Classified on 15 December 1948, and the family stayed.** *The «deux enfants» are the two children in Luiza's photograph.* *(doc.)*
holder: Arolsen Archives
note: **Arolsen Archives**, French-zone IRO records for the Reutlingen–Pfullingen camps, file **148.902**. Supplied by David, 23 September 2026.

title: Zdravko's identity card, Neuhausen 1948
caption:
**Carte d'identité de Personnes Déplacées**, **27 November 1948** — the same day as Luiza's. Nom **DEFRANCESKI**, prénom **Sdrafko**, **Neuhausen, Friedrichstr. 4, Cercle de Reutlingen**, né à **Crikvenica, Yougoslavie**, **auto-mécanicien**, marié. Taille 175, visage ovale, yeux bruns, cheveux châtain.

**Two households of the name in one small town**: Petar and Luiza at *Kelterstr. 30*, Zdravko and Ruža at *Friedrichstr. 4*. **Three months later Zdravko sailed for Australia.** *(doc.)*
holder: Arolsen Archives
note: **Arolsen Archives**, French-zone IRO records for the Reutlingen–Pfullingen camps, file **148.902**. Supplied by David, 23 September 2026.

title: Maria Rosalia Defranceschi, baptised 20 July 1789
caption: Gologorica baptisms, image M01069020. Reading across: the officiant «a.R.D. title: «gratis» — the register says which burials were not paid for
caption: Gologorica deaths, image M01069246, page 35, 1811. Under the officiant's name on three consecutive entries — houses 83, 34 and 93 — the parish priest has written «gratis». title: «Leonardus Defranceschi, civis» — house 5, 1848, aged eighty-two

title: «ex expositis» and «variolae spuriae» — two words on one page, 1853

title: «Deprato» and «Defranceschi» four months apart, in one hand — and the second dies in the first's house

After the household blocks end at «Zajz Giurando N.º 115» the compiler lists six people who died in the parish and did not belong to it, each with where they came from and the page they are on: «Gherscovich Oliva vid.ᵃ ex Cerovglie» (p. 4), the illegitimate twins «Jacobus et Andreas Callagaz … ex Cherbune» (p. 13), «Ausul Maria … ex Gradigne» (p. 15), «Afflich Michael Andrejevich ex Paas» (p. 41), «Chiuch Petrus furlanus ex Castro ⟨—⟩otti fossor» (p. 48), and «Radde Lucia … ex territorio Cherbune nata Bora‹›ıcich q.m Joannis» (p. 53). Krbune twice; Cerovlje once; one Friulian. Three of the six are on famine-year pages. The word «furlanus» appears here and not in the register entry itself.
